## Claims
- [source-backed] For every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\) in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- [source-backed] The source identifies the right-adjoined family as the conjugate family and notes that transposition would prove its minimality, without stating that result as a corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- [source-backed] The involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution and preserves Littlewood–Richardson coefficients under partition conjugation. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 481-491]
- [proved] The right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) minimally generates \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) for every bigrassmannian parameter tuple.

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\), and define
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t).
\]
The bigrassmannian inequalities for \(v^\vee=v_{r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee,n}\) follow from
\[
t^\vee>0,\quad t^\vee\le q,\quad t^\vee\le n-s,\quad
t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0.
\]
Its parameters are
\[
i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad a^\vee=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
\]

By Schur conjugation,
\[
\omega:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\qquad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'},
\]
since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\) iff \(\lambda'\subseteq r^q\). Moreover,
\[
\bigl((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}\bigr)'=(j^i,b^a),
\]
so \(\omega\) bijects the original right-adjoined family with the lower-adjoined family for \(v^\vee\).

If an original right-adjoined element lay in the ideal generated by the remaining right-adjoined elements, applying \(\omega\) would place the corresponding lower-adjoined element for \(v^\vee\) in the ideal generated by its remaining lower-adjoined elements. This contradicts the cited lower-family minimality theorem. Hence the right-adjoined family is minimal. Its generation is the transposed RWY generating result identified in the cited remark.

## Gaps
None for this right-family minimality argument. This does not claim a new source-stated right-family theorem; it supplies an internal proof from the lower-family theorem and conjugation.

## Next
The selected target—universal minimality of the right-adjoined family—was established.
